meta.scope: AWS accounts prod and shared, GCP project acme-prod; environments prod and staging
meta.method: Static review of Terraform and plan JSON; no cloud API calls

inputs.note: Terraform for prod, staging and shared
exported by the requester with terraform show -json

not_run: Terraform dynamic block not evaluated; affected checks not run: envs/prod/aws/sg.tf:20

attack_paths.entry: Internet, through a code-execution or SSRF flaw in the api service
edges: ALB → ECS service api; task security group allows 8080 from the ALB group (modules/service/sg.tf:22)
Task role api-task holds secretsmanager:GetSecretValue on * (modules/service/iam.tf:31)
Secret prod/db/master has no resource policy narrowing readers (envs/prod/aws/secrets.tf:5)

attack_paths.entry: Any GitHub Actions workflow in any repository on github.com
attack_paths.target: Terraform state bucket acme-tfstate and admin of the shared account
edges: Role terraform-deploy trust checks the audience only, no subject condition (envs/shared/aws/oidc.tf:18-34)
State bucket acme-tfstate is readable by the role (envs/shared/aws/state.tf:9)
Internet → database subnet: no route, subnets are private (envs/prod/aws/vpc.tf:40)
Database publicly_accessible is overridden to false in prod (envs/prod/aws/rds.tf:8)
attack_paths.note: Blocked at the database: publicly_accessible = false and private subnets only.

edges: Internet → GCS bucket acme-customer-exports via the public storage endpoint (envs/prod/gcp/storage.tf:3)

attack_paths.note: UNKNOWN: the prod value of var.admin_cidrs is not in the repository

findings.title: Customer export bucket is readable by allUsers
findings.actor: Anyone on the internet; no account needed
findings.path:
1. Bucket acme-customer-exports grants roles/storage.objectViewer to allUsers (envs/prod/gcp/storage.tf:27)
2. Public access prevention is not enforced on the bucket (envs/prod/gcp/storage.tf:3)
3. No organization policy constraints/storage.publicAccessPrevention in the inputs (envs/shared/gcp/org.tf:1)
findings.impact: Expected: customer exports readable only by the export service. Actual: every object is readable by anyone who knows or guesses its name.
findings.fix: Remove the allUsers binding and set public_access_prevention = "enforced"; serve exports through signed URLs.
findings.regression: Policy test: no google_storage_bucket_iam_* member equals allUsers or allAuthenticatedUsers; every bucket sets public_access_prevention = enforced.
controls: CIS GCP Foundation — Cloud Storage buckets are not publicly accessible

validation.evidence: Binding and bucket read end to end at the cited lines; no org policy or VPC-SC perimeter in the inputs.

findings.title: GitHub OIDC deploy role trusts every repository on github.com
findings.actor: Any GitHub user who can run a workflow in a repository they control
findings.path:
1. Workflow requests an OIDC token with audience sts.amazonaws.com (envs/shared/aws/oidc.tf:3)
2. Trust policy conditions only on the aud claim; no sub condition (envs/shared/aws/oidc.tf:18-34)
3. Role has AdministratorAccess (envs/shared/aws/oidc.tf:40)
findings.contrast: none: no other role trusts the GitHub OIDC provider
findings.impact: Expected: only acme/infra on the main branch may assume terraform-deploy. Actual: any repository can, gaining admin of the shared account and the Terraform state.
findings.fix: Add a StringEquals condition on token.actions.githubusercontent.com:sub for repo:acme/infra:ref:refs/heads/main (or its environment).
findings.regression: Policy test: every role trusting the GitHub OIDC provider has a sub condition without wildcards in the organization or repository part.
controls: CIS AWS Foundations — no IAM policy grants full *:* admin privileges

validation.evidence: Trust policy read in full; no permission boundary or SCP in the inputs restricts the role.

findings.title: RDS module defaults to publicly accessible
findings.path:
1. Module variable publicly_accessible defaults to true (modules/db/variables.tf:12)
2. Prod instance uses the module (envs/prod/aws/rds.tf:8)
findings.impact: Expected: database reachable only from the application subnets. Suspected: a public endpoint.
findings.fix: Change the module default to false so new callers are private by default.
findings.regression: Policy test: aws_db_instance.publicly_accessible is false in every plan.
controls: CIS AWS Foundations — RDS instances are not publicly accessible

validation.evidence: Prod overrides publicly_accessible = false at envs/prod/aws/rds.tf:8 and the plan shows false; subnets are private (envs/prod/aws/vpc.tf:40).

findings.title: GKE control plane authorized networks come from an unset variable
findings.actor: Internet, if the deployed CIDR list is broad
findings.path:
1. Cluster has a public endpoint (envs/prod/gcp/gke.tf:9)
2. master_authorized_networks_config takes var.admin_cidrs, which has no default (envs/prod/gcp/variables.tf:4)
findings.contrast: none: the staging cluster also takes its networks from a variable
findings.condition: var.admin_cidrs in prod includes 0.0.0.0/0 or a broad range; its value is not in the repository
findings.impact: Expected: the API server reachable only from the admin VPN. If the condition holds, the API server is reachable from the internet and protected by authentication alone.
findings.fix: Enable a private endpoint, or validate var.admin_cidrs to reject 0.0.0.0/0 and ranges wider than /24.
findings.regression: Policy test: master_authorized_networks_config never contains 0.0.0.0/0; variable validation rejects it.
controls: CIS GKE — control plane authorized networks are enabled

validation.evidence: The variable value lives in the pipeline; requested from the owner.

findings.title: api task role can read every secret in the account
findings.actor: An attacker with code execution in the internet-facing api task
findings.path:
1. ALB exposes the api service on 443 (envs/prod/aws/alb.tf:14)
2. Task role policy grants secretsmanager:GetSecretValue on * (modules/service/iam.tf:31)
3. Secret prod/db/master has no resource policy (envs/prod/aws/secrets.tf:5)
findings.contrast: The worker task role scopes GetSecretValue to prod/worker/* (modules/service/iam.tf:52)
findings.impact: Expected: api reads only its own secrets. Actual: a compromise of api yields every secret, including the database master credential.
findings.fix: Scope the statement to arn:aws:secretsmanager:*:*:secret:prod/api/* and add resource policies on crown-jewel secrets.
findings.regression: Policy test: no task role policy grants secretsmanager:GetSecretValue with Resource "*".
controls: AWS Foundational Security Best Practices — IAM policies do not allow wildcard actions on services

validation.evidence: Role, policy and attachment read at the cited lines; no permission boundary on the role.

findings.title: Production VPC has no flow logs
findings.actor: Not an attack path; limits investigation of AP-01
findings.path: 1. aws_vpc.prod is declared without an aws_flow_log (envs/prod/aws/vpc.tf:1)
findings.contrast: none: no VPC in the inputs has flow logs
findings.impact: Expected: network flows recorded for incident scoping. Actual: none recorded.
findings.fix: Add aws_flow_log for aws_vpc.prod to the central log archive bucket.
findings.regression: Policy test: every aws_vpc has an aws_flow_log referencing it.
controls: CIS AWS Foundations — VPC flow logging is enabled

validation.evidence: No aws_flow_log anywhere in the inputs.

findings.title: Security group allows internet ingress to an admin or data port
controls: CIS AWS Foundations — no security group allows 0.0.0.0/0 to admin ports
CIS AWS Foundations — no security group allows ::/0 to admin ports

validation.evidence: Staging bastion has a public IP; the bastion role is read-only in staging.

findings.title: Instance metadata service does not require IMDSv2
controls: CIS AWS Foundations — EC2 metadata service requires IMDSv2

validation.evidence: envs/staging/aws/bastion.tf:30 has no metadata_options and the instance has a public IP; the bastion role is read-only, so no path to a crown jewel.

findings.title: Basic role roles/owner or roles/editor granted
controls: CIS GCP Foundation — service accounts hold no admin or basic roles

validation.evidence: Every VM without its own service account inherits editor on acme-prod.
